title: Why give material: the job a sacrifice does
outcomes: Names the job of a sacrifice (decoy, or removing a guard) and states the payoff that pays for it
Counts the king's flight squares and the pieces that can recapture before giving anything up
Tells a sacrifice that fails from one that works after a single change to the position
Notices when no sacrifice is needed because the material can be won for free

steps.text:
A **sacrifice** gives up material for something you can name. Two jobs to look for first.
**Decoy:** lure a piece to a square where it hurts its own side.
**Remove a guard:** take or drive off the piece that guards a key square.
Some sacrifices do both jobs at once; say which one you would name first. No named job and payoff means you are guessing. Opening lines against a king: 'The Greek gift: when the bishop sacrifice on h7 works, and when it does not'.

steps.caption: White to move. A decoy: the queen is given up to pull the rook onto g8.

line.say: The queen goes to g8 with check. The knight on h6 guards g8, so the king cannot take it.
The rook takes the queen and now stands next to its own king.

claims.statement: Qg8+ Rxg8 Nf7 is a forced mate in two.
After Qg8+ one white piece (the knight) guards g8.

steps.prompt: Name the job in your own words, then pick the closest option, and give the payoff.

fields.label: The job:
options: Decoy: a piece is lured to a bad square
Remove a guard: a defender is taken or driven off

steps.text:
**When a sacrifice holds.** The payoff must survive Black's best reply, including declining. *Rule of thumb:* count the king's flight squares and the pieces that can recapture before you give anything.
**When it fails.** One flight square, or one extra recapturing piece, can turn a mate into a lost queen.
**When it is not needed.** If the material can be won without giving anything up, win it that way.

steps.title: Same position, one change
steps.prompt: In the first position White has a queen sacrifice: the queen takes the rook that guards f8. Then one thing is changed. Predict for each: sacrifice that works, sacrifice that fails, or no sacrifice at all?
Think of the sacrifice you judged last. Which was missing or vague: its job, its payoff, or the reply that refutes it? How sure were you of your answer? (low / medium / high)
